ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Tremble.cs:21-24) == cost 1 / SKILL / COMMON / ANY_ENEMY -- another enemy-targeting Skill, like card/taunt, card/dominate and card/dark_shackles.

OnPlay.issue: C# applies the debuff unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that DEAD creatures can still receive powers -- it refuses only for a REMOVED corpse. The two agree for an ordinary kill (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, removal at 523-525) and diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower, which draws on any Vulnerable its owner applies with no liveness test on the target (ViciousPower.cs:19-26) -- and card/vicious, audited in this same batch, is its ported source. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE. Note this card has NO damage step at all, so the guard is even less justified here than on the attack+debuff cards: nothing in Tremble's own resolution can kill or remove the target, so the only way the guard fires is if the target was ALREADY a removal-vetoed corpse when the card was played -- which the sim's own `ctx.resolve_target` would have to have selected. Recorded with the same verdict for consistency (rule 3); its reachability is narrower than card/bash's. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (29) and the Vulnerable hover tip (19).
